explainedBy: Cause and effect in the puppy story: the owner gives no guidance, so an accident follows and then a violent reprimand.

storyboard.claim: A new puppy is ignored and never taught where to go.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: ignored, accident, zapped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the dog training example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the neglect-to-punishment chain the narration describes in order.

explainedBy: Time passes with no training, until the inevitable accident on the rug.

storyboard.claim: Three days go by with no training and the dog has an accident.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock, for the passage of days.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The flow is replaced by the waiting period before the accident.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the delay visible: the dog was never taught in those days.

explainedBy: The owner's reaction is a violent punishment of the dog, not teaching.
noVisual: Physical violence is not drawn; the callout names the act and nothing is staged on screen.

storyboard.claim: The owner reacts with violent punishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure is drawn; the callout names the act.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The accident leads to the reprimand.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the violence is only named, the rig cannot draw it.

callout.text: The dog is thrown out the window

explainedBy: The punishment ends with the dog being thrown out of a window, an escape route the dog will learn.

storyboard.claim: The owner throws the dog out a window.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The callout alone; no figure in frame.
storyboard.onScreenText: The dog is thrown out the window
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The punishment continues.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the exit the dog later uses.

explainedBy: The narrator asks what the dog's brain actually learns from the sequence.

storyboard.claim: The question: what does the dog learn from this?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb, the idea of learning, with the question as label.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the punishment, the question turns to learning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks the turn from event to lesson.

explainedBy: The dog learns the punishment sequence: an accident on the rug, then an exit by the window.

storyboard.claim: The dog learns the sequence of the punishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-step flow: rug, then window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Question answered: the lesson is the escape route.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the learned sequence as cause and effect.

explainedBy: The dog never learns the correct behavior because no goal was ever defined.

storyboard.claim: The owner never defined the goal, so nothing correct is learned.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon for the missing goal, with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The learned sequence is set against the missing lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target is the goal that was never set.

explainedBy: The corporate version: a manager leaves people alone until they fail, then zaps them with a furious reprimand.

storyboard.claim: Leave alone zap: leave people alone, then zap them when they fail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee, afraid, in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The dog example maps onto the workplace.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a person in the office under the threat of the zap.

explainedBy: Leave alone zap teaches evasion, not great work.

storyboard.claim: The style teaches evasion, not great work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee walking away in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from the zap style to its result.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the employee avoiding the manager.

explainedBy: Employees avoid the manager, hide mistakes and bury bad data.

storyboard.claim: Employees hide mistakes and bury bad data.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask, a false public face, with the employee holding notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Evasion becomes concrete behavior.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask says they pretend; the notes are the bad data.

explainedBy: The result is a culture of fear, minimal compliance and anxiety.

storyboard.claim: The result is fear and anxiety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee, afraid and slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The behavior becomes a culture.
storyboard.addedInformation: A face of fear fits the claim.

explainedBy: The example that follows is a geography test given by a teacher.

storyboard.claim: A teacher gives a geography test.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book as the test.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new example begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the test; the book stands for the test.

explainedBy: The manager asks why the kids cannot use atlases or maps during the test.

storyboard.claim: Students could use maps in the test.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A compass for maps and direction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The test becomes the question about maps.
storyboard.addedInformation: The compass stands for maps and finding the way.

explainedBy: The teacher refuses outright to let them use maps; the refusal is horrified.

storyboard.claim: The teacher refuses to allow maps.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, angry, pointing in refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question becomes a refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry face shows the threat of the refusal.

explainedBy: Everyone getting 100 percent is treated as a catastrophe.

storyboard.claim: Everyone succeeding is treated as failure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same manager, still pointing, same stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; the reason for the refusal is stated.
storyboard.addedInformation: Only the label changes: the refusal is a rejection of success.

explainedBy: The mindset is a pathological idea that infects modern business.

storyboard.claim: A pathological mindset infects business.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The callout alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The refusal becomes a general mindset.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text carries the claim; nothing in the vocabulary shows an infection.

explainedBy: The stack ranking sorts employees into buckets, the vitality curve at GE.

storyboard.claim: Stack ranking sorts people into top, middle and bottom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with three buckets.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mindset becomes a ranking system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Buckets show the structure of the ranking.

explainedBy: The bell curve needs ten percent of the team to fail so the A grades look legitimate.

storyboard.claim: Ten percent must fail for the curve.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The callout alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sorter gets a specific quota.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ten percent figure comes from the narration.

explainedBy: Managers hide the maps and goals so that success becomes a guessing game.

storyboard.claim: Managers hide the goals and make success a guessing game.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, smirking, holding the notes close.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ranking is run by hiding goals.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk is the manager's charm with an edge.

explainedBy: The question: is micromanaging worse than leaving people alone?

storyboard.claim: The question asks whether micromanaging is worse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee, worried, in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The alternative is raised.
storyboard.addedInformation: The worried face shows the doubt.

explainedBy: Modern employees want autonomy and hate being hovered over.

storyboard.claim: Employees want autonomy and hate hovering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young employee, same stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; the reason is stated.
storyboard.addedInformation: Only the label changes.

explainedBy: Constant praise checks may suffocate employees, treating them like children.

storyboard.claim: Constant check-ins suffocate employees.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager and the young employee in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question becomes the manager's own check-ins.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the two figures show the relation, the callout carries the word.

explainedBy: The distinction is between leaving people alone and suffocating them, weighed against each other.

storyboard.claim: There is a vital distinction to make.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance, two sides weighed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the question with a distinction.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance shows two sides being weighed.

explainedBy: Winners are established high performers who have mastered their role; they are left alone.

storyboard.claim: Proven high performers are the winners who get autonomy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul celebrating with a trophy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The distinction is applied to winners.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy shows the proven performer as a winner.

explainedBy: Give the winner a one-page goal, ensure alignment, then get out of the way.

storyboard.claim: Give the one-page goal and then leave them alone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager holding the one-page goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The winner gets the goal and freedom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes are the one-page goal.

explainedBy: Learners are new or newly promoted and still in the learning phase.

storyboard.claim: The learner is new or stretched.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee, worried, in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The alternative for learners begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the learner's unease.

explainedBy: For a learner, leaving them alone is abandonment, an ambush because they do not know where the pins are.
noVisual: An ambush has no icon in the vocabulary; the callout carries the claim.

storyboard.claim: Leaving a learner alone is abandonment, not autonomy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The afraid young employee.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The learner's case is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the ambush is only text.

explainedBy: Leaving a learner alone is like a pitch black room where they bump into the furniture.

storyboard.claim: The learner is left in the dark and bumps into things.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee falling, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ambush becomes the dark room.
storyboard.addedInformation: The falling pose shows the bump.

explainedBy: Without clear guiding moments, the learner's direction keeps changing into chaos.

storyboard.claim: Without guidance the learner is in chaos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A compass spinning, the learner afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The result of the missing guidance.
storyboard.addedInformation: The spinning compass shows uselessly changing direction.

callout.text: They need to see success clearly

explainedBy: Learners want to know what success looks like: the target.

storyboard.claim: They want to know what success looks like.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target for the success they want to see.
storyboard.onScreenText: They need to see success clearly
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The learner's need is stated.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target is the success goal.

explainedBy: The scene moves to a bowling alley on a Friday night, the system working well.

storyboard.claim: The contrast begins at the bowling alley.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John in the bowling room, neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast with the nightmare.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bowling room sets the new scene.

explainedBy: The classic problem employee is disengaged.

storyboard.claim: The problem employee is disengaged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John, blank, in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bowling scene is replaced by the office.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face shows apathy.

explainedBy: He does the bare minimum, complaining about the coffee and taking long lunches.

storyboard.claim: He does the bare minimum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John holding a coffee cup, slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage: the cup is the coffee he complains about.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cup is the coffee he complains about.

explainedBy: He is actively hostile and drains the energy from the room.

storyboard.claim: He is actively hostile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John, angry, with the cup.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage; the face turns hostile.
storyboard.addedInformation: Only the face and label change.

explainedBy: At the bowling alley he rolls a strike and celebrates.

storyboard.claim: He rolls a strike and celebrates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John celebrating in the bowling room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The same man, now engaged.
storyboard.addedInformation: The celebrate pose is the engaged state.

explainedBy: He chest bumps his teammates, analyzing his form, fully engaged.

storyboard.claim: He is fully engaged with his teammates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John and Paul in a chest bump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The celebration becomes a team moment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The embrace shows two engaged teammates.

explainedBy: The sheet is lifted, so he sees the pins fall at once: instant feedback.

storyboard.claim: The sheet is lifted, so feedback is instant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target and John, surprised, at the lanes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reason for the engagement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target shows the result he can see.

explainedBy: People genuinely want to win.

storyboard.claim: People genuinely want to win.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy with John celebrating.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The insight from the bowling scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy shows the win.

explainedBy: If the sheet is lifted and people see the target and know instantly, they manage themselves.

storyboard.claim: Visible target and instant feedback lead to self-management.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: see target, know instantly, self-manage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The insight becomes the principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause-and-effect chain.

explainedBy: Accurate timely feedback is the top motivator, and once a baseline is met motivation takes care of itself.

storyboard.claim: Feedback is the top motivator; motivation then takes care of itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John celebrating in the bowling room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The chain ends with motivation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The celebrating pose stands for the motivated result.
